desert_p02_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_001.text: The next morning Yue woke before the shopkeeper opened his shutters. Below her window a donkey objected to the existence of morning. She washed her face with the water left in her bowl and went down carrying her plate. The shopkeeper's daughter was asleep at the counter with a brush still in her hand. A column of sums ended in a small drawing of a beetle. Yue set the plate beside it without waking her. Outside, the street smelled of wet stone, yeast, and the first charcoal fires. The caravan yard was already calling for someone called Long Legs.

desert_p02_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_002.text: Long Legs proved to be the shortest driver, a cheerful man who stood on an overturned bucket to inspect a roof strap. He introduced himself by pointing at the bucket. His proper name, he explained, belonged to his mother and the tax office. The road had made other arrangements. Yue asked whether all the drivers had such names. He said only those who had done something foolish in front of witnesses. He climbed down, caught the bucket before it rolled, and asked her to keep that last part between them. She promised nothing while another driver laughed behind a cart.

desert_p02_003.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p02_003.text: Let me see your hands before you pick anything up. The clean water is in that covered basin; the uncovered one belongs to the harness maker, who has exciting opinions about grease. You have slept? Good. Yesterday you said they hurt when you bent the fingers. Bend them slowly now, without trying to impress me. That edge is closing. This patch will want another dressing. You may hold a light staff today. You may write. You will leave ropes, axle jacks, and heavy shutters to people whose palms have not been introduced to a runaway cart.

desert_p02_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_004.text: Yue watched Bao tie the fresh dressing with the knot at the back of her hand. The clinician asked about her old shoulder, then pressed the muscles while Yue moved her arm through the familiar range. There was stiffness from sleeping badly, no return of the deep strain. Bao wrote a short note for Gao and folded it so the paper itself became an envelope. Her covered cup stood beside a spoon and an unfinished letter. When a mule brayed, she glanced at the cup as if checking whether the animal had somehow stolen its contents through the wall.

desert_p02_005.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p02_005.text: You will carry this staff, this case of flags, and the little shoulder bag. The flags are mine; return them even if you grow fond of one. The bag has chalk, a dry cloth, a spare pencil, and a folding shade. Your own notebook can stay in your pack until a page is needed. We have prepared field books that fit the work. See the two columns? What we saw goes here. What we inferred goes there. I spent three years pretending I could remember the distinction later. Du spent those years enjoying the results far too much.

desert_p02_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_006.text: The light staff was ash with a brass cap, longer than Yue was tall and balanced a little below its midpoint. She tried it at three lengths before finding a grip that left her bandages clear. Gao altered the shoulder strap and marked the new hole with chalk. Nothing was presented as a reward. Each borrowed thing had been used by somebody else, worn at the places where that person's habits had pressed. Yue liked the bag's softened leather. Inside the flag case she found a note advising the next assistant never to lend the red flag to a cook.

desert_p02_007.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_007.text: The cook saw the note and demanded to know whether it was signed. Gao said that guilt required no signature. He took a red cloth from his pocket, much smaller than a survey flag, and explained that somebody had to stop flour blowing into the beans. A driver called across the yard that the flour had improved them. The cook bowed gravely toward the praise and asked for the man's bowl back so that he could test an even better recipe. Yue fastened the flag case and decided that a caravan's reputation could never be fully explained by its employer.

desert_p02_008.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p02_008.text: Your sandals are ordinary enough. That is praise. People arrive with heels intended to conquer the basin and discover that the basin eats heels. Turn your foot. This strap rubs here when leather swells. Wet it, walk the length of the yard, then tell me where it hurts. Do not let the shoemaker hear you saying it merely feels different; he can survive an honest complaint. He once sold me two right soles and argued that I was walking toward the wrong horizon. I still buy his leather. I make him lay both feet on the counter first.

desert_p02_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_009.text: The wet strap rubbed exactly where Tuo had pointed. Yue returned to the stall outside, where the shoemaker shaved the inside edge and punched another hole. He looked at the dressing on her palm and asked whether the cart had been worth saving. She said the people beside it had been. He grunted and charged for the new leather, leaving the adjustment free because Tuo had already paid him to examine the crew's footwear. A girl behind the stool counted the coins into a tin and asked whether Yue would bring back a white stone shaped like a fish.

desert_p02_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_010.text: Yue said she would look for one near a safe stopping place, and the girl described a fish with teeth. The shoemaker corrected her request to something that could fit in a pocket. On the way back Yue found Han beside three sacks. He was testing the seams with his thumb, his coat hanging from a peg behind him. A stitch broke. He set that sack aside, swore once, and asked a worker to fetch its maker before the shop grew crowded. The worker said this had been the expensive batch. Han's expression suggested that fact was precisely the problem.

desert_p02_011.speaker: han_xun
desert_p02_011.text: There are days when I think the road carries goods between towns chiefly to teach towns what they have sold us. Those sacks held meal for a roofless shed. Wind gets through a weak seam more easily than a bad argument. We will take sound ones. The maker may repair these for the next journey if he wishes. You need a cloak too. The issue chest is under the canopy. Try it sitting as well as standing. Last season a man chose one by admiring his reflection; he spent three days looking magnificent while unable to reach his own bowl.

desert_p02_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_012.text: The issue chest contained repaired cloaks, broad hats, dark eye screens, and spare cloth wraps. Yue chose a pale cloak with a patch at the knee and a hat whose lining could be washed. Gao showed her how the screens lifted away from the face for close reading. She copied their issue marks into the field book. A driver helped her fit the pack beneath the cloak without trapping its straps. His own pack held a wooden bird, wrapped in an old sock, which he refused to explain until they had travelled far enough for his story to improve.

desert_p02_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_013.text: A watchman arrived from the gate with a notice and milk somebody had pressed on him while he waited. Tuo read the notice standing with one foot on the lowest rail. The Black Gate opened at first light, closed during repair at noon, and admitted loaded carts by the narrower eastern arch. Yesterday's measurements would suffice. The western arch had lost another stone overnight. Tuo asked whether people remained beneath it. The watchman said the mason had cleared both stalls and was waiting for braces. She offered him the yard's spare rope, then told Han where it was going.

desert_p02_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_014.text: Han entered the rope loan beside the sacks rather than making the watchman wait for a second signature. He asked for its return before the next caravan departed, not before this one. Yue listened to the easy difference between those dates. In the distance a hammer rang against the gate wall. The sound travelled over the houses cheerfully, though somebody would lose a day's trade beneath the closed arch. Gao unfolded the updated width sketch and tested the tool rack again. It folded cleanly. One driver asked whether they could now persuade the mules to fold as well.

desert_p02_015.speaker: du_she
desert_p02_015.text: They do fold. Usually at the moment when a passenger has chosen to put his only decent coat beside them. Give me the field book, Yue. I want to show you the northern page before dust turns every pencil mark into a family resemblance. We measured this line from the old market stone. The new distance begins at the cistern door. I have marked the gap in both copies. If you find a road marker that contradicts either, sketch the marker before arguing with the map. Stone is often wrong for an interesting reason. Paper is wrong for cheaper ones.

desert_p02_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_016.text: He had redrawn the page overnight with the older origin left visible beneath a crossing line. Yue asked whether people using the first edition would receive the correction. Du tapped a stack of small slips tied with blue thread. Han would leave them with the receiving houses that stocked his sheets. It would not reach everybody, he admitted. For that reason the next printing would carry the date more prominently. Gao passed behind him, read the top slip, and said the correction was plain. Du pretended to examine his spectacles while accepting the compliment. His ears coloured above the frames.

desert_p02_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_017.text: Nearby two drivers argued over a spare wheel. One wanted it strapped high where it would not collect dust; the other pointed out that unloading it would require the heaviest lift at the worst moment. Yue had been asked to record placement, not settle the quarrel. She waited until Gao joined them. The surveyor had the wheel lowered against the cart frame, clear of the brake line. Both drivers immediately claimed this had been their intention. Gao gave them opposite ends of the securing strap. The wheel stayed quiet after that, which seemed to Yue an adequate verdict.

desert_p02_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_018.text: The third cart carried the field equipment and part of the water. Its driver unrolled the padding for Gao's tripod with a tenderness usually reserved for sleeping children. Gao said the tenderness came from having paid for a bent leg once. Under the cloth lay an ordinary levelling head, a plumb bob, sighting bars, and two graduated rods. The reference stone remained in a separate locked box in Gao's own bag. Yue recognised the instrument from yesterday's room but not the adjustment knobs. She wrote their names beside small sketches, leaving space for the mistakes she expected to make.

desert_p02_019.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p02_019.text: This screw settles the bubble. This one changes the sight. Confuse them and you will spend an afternoon bringing the horizon down to your pencil. We practise on the yard because the yard is willing to wait. Sight that nail in the wall. Tell me when the image stops wandering. No hurry. Dust on the lens can resemble a very distant bird, and somebody once reported a flock of birds that followed our caravan for two days. I am not telling you who. If Du asks, tell him you admire the consistency of his observations.

desert_p02_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_020.text: The nail shifted whenever Yue pressed too hard against the sighting frame. She rested her wrist, tried again, and found it steady. Gao moved the staff twice, checked the readings herself, and let Yue copy the figures before explaining the small discrepancy. Sunlight warmed the wall unevenly; the staff's shaded face and bright face had not settled together. They put it beneath the canopy while the drivers finished loading. Yue had thought careful work would feel like holding herself rigid. Instead it involved learning when to stop touching things. This struck her as a useful lesson beyond surveying.

desert_p02_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_021.text: At breakfast Bao took one look at the field book and told Yue to loosen her shoulders. The cook had made a breakfast stew that seemed largely designed to persuade people they had eaten last night's beans in a new way. Han arrived with the repaired sack maker, who accepted a bowl before defending his thread. The cook asked which was stronger, the thread or the argument. The maker chose thread, produced a sound seam for inspection, and promised replacements before dusk. Han gave him a receipt with the rejected batch clearly listed. They finished breakfast without becoming enemies.

desert_p02_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_022.text: After the bowls were cleared, the farrier brought out the six mule records and placed them where Tuo could read without taking off her hat. Each animal had a name, a recent weight, the condition of its feet, and a tendency considered unjust. One disliked blue sleeves. One liked to bite ropes belonging to people who looked busy. The largest, a grey female with a torn ear, allowed Yue to scratch beneath her jaw, then searched her pockets. Tuo said affection on the road could be measured accurately in grain. Yue moved the flag case beyond the muzzle's reach.

desert_p02_023.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p02_023.text: That one is Plum. Do not offer your fingers as proof of friendship. She takes proof seriously. The thin brown pair belong to the first cart; they work well if the driver remembers which one turns first. These two are sisters. That does not mean they agree about anything. We change the leading pair at the longer rests, and the farrier checks them before the evening feed. If a hoof fails, the cart waits. A bad foot can spoil a road faster than a bad map, though I advise you not to quote that where Du can hear it.

desert_p02_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_024.text: Du was close enough to hear and replied that at least his maps did not kick. The farrier said they had sent more people limping home than Plum ever had. Their laughter drew Plum's ears back. Yue found the animal's record beside the others and noted its old scar before asking whether it limited work. The farrier showed her the healed edge and the examination date. He had cleared Plum for the journey and would travel with the caravan. The scar was not permission to ignore a fresh limp. Yue returned the sheet to its clip without adding a story.

desert_p02_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_025.text: At noon the yard quieted. Workers took their rest in shade that narrowed as the roofs warmed. Han sent the newest driver home to sleep because the man had spent half the night helping the gate mason. Yue sat with Gao beneath the canopy and watched a white moth fail repeatedly to understand the edge of a blue cup. On the contract table a purse lay tied with green cord: the crew's return fare if the carts could not come back. Han had shown its deposit receipt to them at breakfast. It looked disappointingly small for the reassurance it carried.

desert_p02_026.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p02_026.text: You are looking at the purse as though it might grow if you concentrate. We used to carry more silver on the road. Then a flood taught us that a promise held at the receiving house could survive water better than a cart chest. That purse covers immediate expenses; the larger deposit stays here. The receiving keeper has each worker's name. We carry duplicate claims in three packs. If you dislike the arrangement, ask before departure. It is harder to make a clerk explain himself after you have travelled far enough to turn him into a memory.

desert_p02_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_027.text: Yue had already read her name on the claim. She asked how Gao had come home from the flood. The surveyor turned the cup so its handle would stop tempting the moth. She had travelled in a farmer's pig cart with a broken instrument and somebody else's grandmother. The grandmother disliked the pigs; the pigs disliked Gao's boots. They had reached a bridge just before it closed. She kept the boots for another year because replacing them would have felt ungrateful. Yue asked about the grandmother. Gao smiled. She had sent three complaints and a jar of pears.

desert_p02_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_028.text: The reference instrument required a finer arrangement than yesterday's basic sighting lesson. In the workroom Gao set out its graduated test load, a shielded return cup, and the card describing acceptable limits. Bao checked Yue's palms and seated her so neither hand bore weight. The small contact lead rested against an unbroken patch of wrist. Yue could decline without losing the assistant work. She chose one supervised test, expecting its familiar breathing rhythm to make the room feel like the kiln. Instead she heard the yard cart bells and realised that familiarity could travel without making places identical.

desert_p02_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_029.text: Gao performed the first pulse from her reference stone, writing its reading. After a rest, Yue settled the first arm pair and admitted the rated half unit over four breaths. The cup accepted a quarter unit of useful work within the marked band. Gao stopped the test there. Yue released the paired route, waited for the return lead to settle, and described the warmth at her wrist before looking at the scale. Bao asked about pain. There was none. A second task would be unnecessary for hiring, so they let the apparatus cool while ordinary conversation returned.

desert_p02_030.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p02_030.text: Your trained interruption is clean. That qualifies you for this particular light task under my supervision, within today's restrictions. On the road we shall mostly use the reference stone and our eyes. I wanted to see how you responded when a reading did not arrive with somebody cheering beside it. You waited. Keep that. Nothing ruins an observation more beautifully than the desire to make it encouraging. Du has another version of this lecture, but his includes three winters, an accused magistrate, and a dog. Ask him at camp when you are sure the beans will need a long cooking.

desert_p02_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_031.text: Yue copied the test's half-unit expenditure into her private practice notes. The small cost was not alarming, but it belonged to today's body rather than tomorrow's hopes. Gao showed her the instrument's remaining reference charge and closed its padded box. Du waited outside with a paper cone of roasted seeds. He asked whether his lecture had already been slandered. Gao accepted a seed as the fee for not answering. Bao sent them back into the open air and kept Yue long enough to change the contact cloth. The warm patch faded while they discussed the shoemaker's impossible fish request.

desert_p02_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_032.text: By late afternoon the rejected sacks had returned with new stitching, and the maker stood beside them holding a needle as evidence of his occupation. Han tested one seam, loaded another with grain, and authorised payment only after both held. The maker's assistant carried away the failed thread without being blamed for its purchase. Yue helped enter the replacements while the cook checked the grain against his meal plan. He had packed dried greens too, claiming they would surprise the beans. They smelled sharp and pleasant. Outside, the mules stamped in the shade, ready to eat anything except a plan.

desert_p02_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_033.text: The water keeper came when the roofs cast their longest shadows. He carried a measuring rod in a leather sleeve and refused Han's offer of tea until the tanks were finished. Each cart had its own lined reservoir, bolted low between the wheels. The first held six hundred and forty usable litres; the other two held six hundred and twenty apiece. Their cleaning water had already drained into the yard trough. Yue watched the keeper check the interiors, measure the filled depth, and compare it with each tank's stamped table. Empty space above the water was deliberate, not a shortage.

desert_p02_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_034.text: The total was one thousand eight hundred and eighty usable litres, excluding the keeper's rinse bucket and the little water trapped below the outlet. A protected compartment held two hundred within that total. Han sealed its tap with red thread so a broken seal would announce an emergency draw without preventing one. Gao asked Yue to read back the figures. The twelve adults and six mules would need a forecast hundred and sixty-eight litres each ordinary day. Nine days left a margin above the protected amount, but hotter work could eat it. Han listened without offering the weather a contract.

desert_p02_035.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p02_035.text: See this shade panel? We put it where the sun can find the cart, not where it pleases the painter. These tanks travel wrapped. At each long stop the drivers look beneath the frame and touch the joints with a dry cloth. A stain matters even when it is small. If you see one, call the driver before wondering whether somebody else has already noticed. The basin has a way of making people shy about bad news. It is a terrible place to practise courtesy with a leaking cart. I prefer a rude interruption and a full cup.

desert_p02_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_036.text: Yue helped hold the wrapping while a driver fastened it, her fingers on the cloth. The tank smelled faintly of the boiled herb used in its last cleaning. Han had separated the cooking allowance from the crew's drinking portions in the daily plan; both belonged inside the human forecast. The cook inspected the lids and claimed he could make soup that persuaded people to remember drinking. Bao replied that she would inspect that claim personally. She then asked for a smaller covered pot near her seat, filled from the day's allocation when treatment required it, rather than an uncounted gift.

desert_p02_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_037.text: Forty kilograms of charcoal went beneath a weather cover, split between two carts so one overturned load would not leave the whole caravan without cooking fuel. The cook weighed them and marked the tie of each. Beside them sat the folding stove, its feet already blackened by journeys Yue would never know. There were grain, dried greens, salt fish, and a little preserved fruit for the drivers who found hot food difficult at dawn. Han refused a merchant's last-minute crate of glazed cups. The agreed load had room for work, meals, and repair supplies, not a speculative sale.

desert_p02_038.speaker: han_xun
desert_p02_038.text: I could sell the cups at Crescent House if anyone lived there to buy them. The merchant knows that too; he enjoys saying the name as though it were a market town. Once it was a stopping house. Now our customer wants its walls measured and the old approach checked. He pays for a report, not for a tale about treasures behind the plaster. Du's source describes an abandoned roof and a courtyard. Tuo has seen the place from the southern shelf. We shall find out what the years have done to it before selling anybody a cup there.

desert_p02_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_039.text: Yue asked who had ordered the survey. A cooperative of road carriers had subscribed to it after three consignments turned back from conflicting route directions. Han's firm carried two of those loads; another factor carried the third and blamed Han's preferred map. Gao's report would belong to all the subscribers, with a public route summary afterwards. The repair recommendations could be ignored, but the observations would carry her name and date. Han spread the correspondence on the table. Much of it was impolite. He let Yue read the disagreement rather than offering only the letters in which he sounded wise.

desert_p02_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_040.text: One rival sheet placed a spring west of the abandoned house. Du's older edition labelled the same depression a seasonal seep. A recent carrier claimed he had drawn three barrels there, but his statement gave neither month nor barrel size. Tuo knew the depression and would not schedule it as drinking water. Gao circled it for inspection only if the road, time, and safe approach allowed. Yue wrote the uncertainty in the field book. It looked smaller on paper than it would feel under sunlight. The cook read the spring claim, looked at the loaded tanks, and kept packing beans.

desert_p02_041.speaker: du_she
desert_p02_041.text: The rival compiler is a capable woman. I disagree with her spring mark. Those statements can coexist, although Han occasionally hopes they cannot. Her latest note uses the name Long Shadow, while my notes use Hollow Orchard. Names move faster than rocks. We shall carry both, ask people which hollow they mean, and make a sketch from a common place. If it is the same ground, we shall say so. If she is right about water, I shall revise my sheet and spare myself the pleasure of sending hungry travellers to a correct dry hole.

desert_p02_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_042.text: Gao glanced at him over the field book. He noticed, shrugged, and said he had been young for far too long. The rival compiler's name remained in a letter rather than becoming another companion. She had not joined this commission. Du would carry her published sheet and her dated clarification, copied with permission from the receiving house. Yue tied the pages separately from the route notebook so a gust could not make one edition look like another. She had been given a second pencil. She sharpened it while the adults discussed a road she had yet to see.

desert_p02_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_043.text: The loading rehearsal began with every worker standing beside the thing they would handle at a stop. Long Legs stood by the first cart's brake, now repaired and tested. The driver with the wooden bird held the second pair's lead. The third driver, a quiet woman with a laugh that arrived suddenly, had the equipment cart. The cook, farrier, and camp worker checked stove, feet, and shelters. Tuo walked the whole line. Gao watched Yue unpack and set the sighting staff without dragging its cap. Nobody was especially graceful. The objects moved into sensible places, which mattered more.

desert_p02_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_044.text: Then Plum ate a corner of the first cart's load sheet. The driver shouted; the grey mule backed toward the folded shelter with the paper stuck to her lip. Yue moved the staff out of the way and let Tuo take the lead. Pulling the paper would have invited a contest the mule could win. Tuo offered a handful from Plum's measured feed, waited for the jaw to work, and retrieved what remained. The driver stared at the damp ruin of his neat headings. Han brought him the duplicate. Du observed that this edition had received a thorough animal review.

desert_p02_045.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p02_045.text: She is telling you that lists need edges people can reach without asking her permission. Put the clip higher. Yes, there. Now she will have to develop a longer neck before helping with the accounts again. We do not punish her for finding paper where food ought to be. We do keep fingers out of her mouth. Yue, thank you for moving the staff. People often try to rescue everything at once and discover they have brought a horse three new ways to knock them down. Long Legs, stop laughing. Your bucket is still under her nose.

desert_p02_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_046.text: The bucket disappeared behind the first cart just as Plum turned toward it. Long Legs announced that he had always preferred walking. The rehearsal continued around a deliberate narrow gap made from two benches. The folded tool rack cleared it; the last cart's rear strap caught a projecting nail. They stopped, pulled the bench back, and replaced the torn strap. Tuo would inspect the gate jambs before the actual passage, but an imaginary gate had already taught them something useful. Yue wrote the incident beneath the repaired brake. She left out the bucket because its owner's reputation had suffered enough.

desert_p02_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_047.text: The midday heat had passed before Gao sent Yue to collect the last copied route permit from the receiving house. Han gave her the paid claim slip; the clerk gave it back cancelled and handed over the permit. Outside, a woman sold sour plums from a shallow basket. Yue bought a small paper packet and carried it into the yard, where its name caused immediate confusion with the mule. The driver insisted that the animal could not eat herself. The cook claimed this was an unnecessarily ambitious interpretation of lunch. Yue kept two fruits and let the packet travel.

desert_p02_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_048.text: At the receiving house she had also seen a notice for two guides overdue from an eastern traverse. Their families had written the last known stopping place, their intended return date, and a contact address. The route lay away from the caravan's planned approach. Yue copied the notice onto paper, then showed it to Tuo. The guide recognised one surname but had no fresh knowledge of either traveller. They would carry the notice and ask at ordinary stops. Han sent a clerk to leave their departure route with the families, who deserved facts rather than a promise of discovery.

desert_p02_049.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p02_049.text: People get lost in stories before they get found on roads. Someone hears that a guide is late and gives him a broken leg, a quarrel, and a hidden treasure by supper. Take what the notice says. If a traveller offers news, ask where and when they saw them. Those families will hear every rumour in the market whether we help or not. We can at least send a report that does not turn guessing into weather. Your page is dry? Put it inside the flap. There is no virtue in preserving a rumour better than a useful address.

desert_p02_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_050.text: The note about the eastern guides changed Tuo's mood. She stood awhile at the yard wall, looking toward roofs that hid the road. Yue did not ask which surname she knew. After a few minutes the guide returned to the loading line and retied a strap that had passed inspection. Gao approached her with two cups. Tuo accepted one, drank, and handed it back without speaking. Their silence had the ease of people who had quarrelled and found work. Du watched from the map table, then bent over the rival sheet as though the paper required all his attention.

desert_p02_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_051.text: Han's daughter arrived in the early evening carrying a folded shawl and a complaint about the size of his handwriting. Yue had imagined a small child from the drawing of the three wheels. The young woman before her was nearly grown, wearing ink marks on her sleeve. The drawing had been sent years ago and kept through several coats. She introduced herself only as the person who would collect unpaid complaints while he was gone. Han accepted the shawl with the solemnity of a royal appointment. Then he asked whether she had eaten, and she rolled her eyes affectionately.

desert_p02_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_052.text: They sat beside the contract table while the cook reheated soup. Han's daughter had been helping at a school beyond the western ridge and returned because her mother's cough had worsened. Bao asked two quiet questions, heard that another clinician was attending the house, and promised to look in after supper before the departure. The daughter did not ask her father to stay. Instead she took the too-small copy of Yue's agreement and held it against his nose. He said he had already rewritten it. She inspected the fresh page and conceded that civilisation might yet survive him.

desert_p02_053.speaker: han_xun
desert_p02_053.text: She was eight when she drew the cart. I had told her three wheels would be easier to steer. She believed me for about ten minutes, then spent the rest of the day explaining the problem to everybody who entered our house. I kept the drawing because it recorded the exact point at which she became a better engineer than her father. This button was on the coat I wore then. You saw me looking for it yesterday. People think factors count only money. We are very foolish about other small things when nobody has paid us to be sensible.

desert_p02_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_054.text: Yue helped his daughter carry the empty bowls to the cook. The young woman asked what the desert looked like. Yue said she would know when she returned. That answer pleased her more than a description borrowed from somebody else. She mentioned the schoolchildren's white stones and cautioned Yue against accepting too many requests. Her father had once brought home a cart full of rocks, each apparently belonging to a different nephew. The cook called that cargo more digestible than his supplies. Han's daughter laughed, then grew quiet when the yard bell announced the final evening check.

desert_p02_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_055.text: Bao left for Han's house with her medicine bag, keeping enough time to return before the crew's last briefing. Yue swept the eating shelter after her tasks ended and sitting among other people's work felt awkward. Gao let her finish one patch, then told her that rest was part of the job rather than a debt to the cook. They sat outside the canopy as the yard cooled. A boy at the gate practised a tune on a reed pipe, stopping at the same difficult turn every time. Gao began humming the missing notes until he heard and tried again.

desert_p02_056.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p02_056.text: My first field season was full of people telling me to be grateful for work. I was grateful. It made me agree to tasks I could not do well after sunset. Du once found me asleep with my cheek on a distance sheet and refused to let me measure until noon. I resented him terribly. Then I discovered he had measured the wrong corner himself while tired. We can all learn generosity from somebody else's embarrassment if we are willing. Tomorrow you walk in the cool hours. Tonight you sleep enough to notice where you have put your own feet.

desert_p02_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_057.text: Du joined them with the corrected map stack and asked whether his embarrassing corner had received adequate dramatic treatment. Gao said it had been shortened out of kindness. He settled onto the bench with a little grunt his formal manner could not conceal. The reed pipe reached its turn and failed again. Du whistled it accurately without looking at the boy. Gao stared. He said a mapmaker was allowed other accomplishments, especially ones that did not require drawing a coastline. For a few minutes the three of them listened while the boy assembled the tune from their scattered help.

desert_p02_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_058.text: At the briefing Han read the departure hour and the nine-day work plan. Weather, an unsafe road, or an injured animal could alter the dates; Gao and Tuo would advise him before any extension. The gate inspection came first, then the road across the lower plain. No supply at Hollow Orchard had entered the water forecast. Yue looked at the tanks beneath their covers and felt the difference between hoping for a spring and planning without one. The promised report could wait if people needed to turn back. Han said that plainly while Du kept his pen off the paper.

desert_p02_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_059.text: Tuo asked each driver to repeat the stopping signal. They would not use a distant shout alone when wind could carry it away. A red flag and the first cart's halt would tell the others to wait; a driver who lost sight of both stopped rather than searching forward blindly. Yue practised setting the flag where the last cart could see it. In daylight the red cloth looked almost gaudy. At dusk it vanished sooner than she expected. Gao made her walk back and discover that herself, then adjusted departure tasks so packing finished before the sky grew dark.

desert_p02_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_060.text: The camp worker tested the patched tents while the farrier completed a last quiet examination. A driver who had been joking all day became grave when his mule lifted a foot. The farrier found a small stone in the outer groove and removed it without cutting healthy horn. The driver held the animal's head against his shoulder until it settled. Yue recognised Han's gesture from the broken cart, performed here without anybody watching for credit. She had begun the morning thinking chiefly about the instruments. By evening the caravan seemed held together by attention distributed among its people and beasts.

desert_p02_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_061.text: Bao returned after the lamps were lit. Han met her beside the first cart, far enough from the others for his wife's health to remain her own affair. The clinician spoke quietly; his shoulders eased without becoming carefree. He thanked her and went to check the cook's covers. Bao changed Yue's dressing last for the night and approved ordinary staff work in the morning if the healing remained clean. Yue asked whether Han's household needed anything carried from the road. Bao said letters, when possible, and no heroic additions to the cargo. Ordinary news could be a useful medicine.

desert_p02_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_062.text: Yue placed her issued gear beside the habitual pack. The plain sword stayed in its usual sheath, secured where it would not catch a cart strap. The practice lead went beneath her notebook rather than among Gao's instruments; belonging to the same traveller did not make them interchangeable. She counted the two pencils, then smiled at herself for doing it twice. Outside, Han's daughter said farewell to the drivers and promised to report any foolishness they wished to send home. Long Legs asked for a discount. She told him his family had already paid in advance.

desert_p02_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_063.text: The workers' room was louder that night. One man snored before the others had found their blankets; another whispered through the first page of a letter until somebody offered to supply all the words he could not spell. Yue lay beside the window, listening to the help turn into teasing and back again. Her palms throbbed, then eased as she changed their position. She pictured the route lines with their corrected origins, the eastern guides' notice, the tanks waiting beneath cloth. None would become simpler while she watched the ceiling. She let them go for the length of her sleep.

desert_p02_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p02_064.text: Before first light, Tuo knocked once on the door and said the mules were awake enough to make their own decisions if people delayed. Yue dressed by the shielded lamp, folded her blanket, and drank the cup provided from the yard cistern. Breakfast waited in covered bowls near the gate. The caravan's sealed supply had not yet been drawn. Gao stood beside the equipment cart with her hat tied loosely against her back. She saw Yue approaching, handed her the light staff, and pointed toward the dark street. Beyond the roofs, the Black Gate had begun opening for the day.
